speed_note: The first cut cost +2.8%/+4.3% on the two smallest PE loads because decode_named_protos parsed the cspec document a third time. Folding the return-address, default-proto and named-model readers onto ONE parse in build_default_proto removed two of the three parses that existed before this PR and brought the worst-case load delta to +0.5%.
decisions: Lift the existing <default_proto> decode body into a reusable decode_proto_model rather than implementing the marshaling-decoder ProtoModel::decode stub: the <pentry> storage resolution needs the engine Translate and the AddrSpaceManager, which only Architecture has. Reusing one body for the default AND the named models is what guarantees identical storage/effect fidelity.
set_name LAST, so the C++ `if (name == "__thiscall") hasThis = true` override (fspec.cc:2595) wins over an explicit hasthis=false, exactly as upstream orders it.

Skip a named model that fails to decode instead of aborting the spec (upstream throws). kuna's vendored cspec corpus spans every processor it ships; one undecodable named model must not cost the architecture its default one. Census: 0 of 294 language:compiler pairs lose anything.

Do NOT honor <eval_current_prototype>/<eval_called_prototype>. Six cspecs declare one, and honoring it would hand every function on those targets the merged model. That is a default change with its own evidence burden, not registration, and the PR scope forbids changing which model any function gets.

Port the upstream guarantee that every language has a __thiscall model (architecture.cc:1342), cloning it off the default when the spec declares none. It is still pure registration, and the demangler/DWARF follow-up needs getModel(__thiscall) to resolve on more than the x86 family.
No option: registration cannot change emitted C. Proven by the 675/675 ablation and 12 byte-identical whole-binary sweeps, not assumed.
